title.zh: 卷四百十三 列傳第一百七十二 趙汝談 趙汝讜 趙希錧 趙彥吶 趙善湘 趙與懽 趙必愿
title.en: Volume 413 Biographies 172: Zhao Rutan, Zhao Rudang, Zhao Xiguan, Zhao Yanne, Zhao ShanXiang, Zhao Yuhuan, Zhao Biyuan
title.raw: 卷四百十三 列傳第一百七十二 趙汝談 趙汝讜 趙希錧 趙彥吶 趙善湘 趙與懽 趙必愿 Volume 413 Biographies 172: Zhao Rutan, Zhao Rudang, Zhao Xiguan, Zhao Yanne, Zhao ShanXiang, Zhao Yuhuan, Zhao Biyuan

sentences.zh: 趙汝談趙汝讜趙希趙彥呐趙善湘趙與歡趙必願

translations.literal: Zhao Rutan, Zhao Rudang, Zhao Xi, Zhao Yanne, Zhao Shanxiang, Zhao Yuhuan, Zhao Biyuan
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Zhao Rutan, Zhao Rudang, Zhao Xiguan, Zhao Yanne, Zhao Shanxiang, Zhao Yuhuan, and Zhao Biyuan

sentences.zh: 趙汝談，字履常，生而穎悟，年十五，以大父恩補將仕郎。

translations.literal: Zhao Rutan, styled Lüchang, was born quick and perceptive. At age fifteen, through his great-grandfather's favor he was granted the office of Jiangshi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rutan, courtesy name Lüchang, was gifted from birth. At fifteen he received the rank of Gentleman for Meritorious Service through his great-grandfather's privilege.

sentences.zh: 登淳熙十一年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the eleventh year of the Chunxi reign (1184).

sentences.zh: 丞相周必大得其文異之，語參知政事施師點曰：“是子他日有大名於世。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Zhou Bida, finding his writings remarkable, said to Vice Administrator Shi Shidian: 'This youth will one day have a great name in the world.'
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Zhou Bida was struck by his writing and told Vice Administrator Shi Shidian, "This young man will one day be famous throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: ”調汀州教授，改廣德軍，添差江西安撫司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: He was assigned as instructor at Ting Prefecture, transferred to Guangde Army, and given an additional appointment as staff officer of the Jiangxi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as instructor at Ting Prefecture, then transferred to Guangde Army, and given a supplementary appointment on the staff of the Jiangxi Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 嚐從朱熹訂疑義十數條，熹嗟異之。

translations.literal: He once joined Zhu Xi in resolving more than ten doubtful points, and Xi sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He once worked with Zhu Xi to settle more than ten disputed points of interpretation, and Zhu Xi marveled at his ability.

sentences.zh: 佐丞相趙汝愚定大策，汝愚欲驟以詞掖處之，力辭去。

translations.literal: He assisted Chief Councillor Zhao Ruyu in settling a great policy. Ruyu wished abruptly to place him in the Secretariat, but he forcefully declined and left.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Chief Councillor Zhao Ruyu shape a major policy. Ruyu wanted to place him at once in the Secretariat, but he firmly refused and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 持祖母服。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 汝愚去國，其弟汝讜力上疏乞留汝愚、斬侂胄，聞者吐舌。

translations.literal: When Ruyu left the court, his younger brother Rudang forcefully submitted a memorial begging to retain Ruyu and execute Han Tuozhou. Those who heard it stuck out their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu was driven from court, his younger brother Rudang submitted a bold memorial asking that Ruyu be kept and Han Tuozhou be executed. All who heard of it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 兄弟罹黨禍斥去。

translations.literal: The brothers suffered factional disaster and were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers fell victim to factional persecution and were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋調安慶府教授，添差浙東安撫司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred as instructor at Anqing Prefecture and given an additional appointment as staff officer of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as instructor at Anqing Prefecture and given a supplementary post on the staff of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，免喪，召為太社令。

translations.literal: He completed mourning for his mother. When the mourning period ended, he was summoned as Director of the Grand Altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he was recalled and appointed Director of the Grand Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 時侂胄用事熾甚，汝談痛憤，登壇讀祝，大呼侂胄及陳自強名。

translations.literal: At that time Tuozhou's power was extremely rampant. Rutan was deeply pained and indignant. Ascending the altar to read the invocation, he loudly called out the names of Tuozhou and Chen Ziqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou's power was then at its height. Rutan, filled with grief and anger, mounted the altar to read the invocation and loudly pronounced the names of Tuozhou and Chen Ziqiang.

sentences.zh: 自強不能堪，它日指汝談曰：“末坐白皙者何人？

translations.literal: Ziqiang could not bear it. Another day he pointed at Rutan and said: 'Who is that fair-skinned man in the last seat?'
translations.idiomatic: Ziqiang could not endure the affront. On another occasion he pointed at Rutan and asked, "Who is that pale-faced man seated at the end?"

sentences.zh: ”汝談不為動。

translations.literal: Rutan was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan remained unmoved.

sentences.zh: 以參知政事李壁薦，召試館職，擢正字。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Vice Administrator Li Bi, he was summoned to a trial appointment in the Academy and promoted to Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Vice Administrator Li Bi, he was summoned to a qualifying examination for an Academy post and promoted to Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 是時吳曦叛，上下束手，或請就以曦為王，其人造汝談，汝談詰之曰：“孰欲王曦者，可斬！

translations.literal: At that time Wu Xi rebelled, and the court was at a loss. Some proposed making Xi a king. A man came to Rutan, who interrogated him, saying: 'Whoever wishes to make Xi king may be executed!'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Xi had rebelled, and the court was helpless. Some suggested making Xi a king. When a man came to Rutan with this proposal, Rutan challenged him: "Whoever would make Xi a king deserves execution!"

sentences.zh: ”其人麵發赤不能對，遂以言去，主管崇道觀。

translations.literal: The man's face turned red and he could not reply. Rutan then left office on account of his words and was made superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: The man flushed and could not answer. Rutan was then dismissed because of his outspokenness and appointed superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 添差通判嘉興府，與郡守王介誌合。

translations.literal: He was given an additional appointment as vice prefect of Jiaxing Prefecture and found himself in accord with the prefect Wang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He received a supplementary appointment as vice prefect of Jiaxing Prefecture, where he and Prefect Wang Jie saw eye to eye.

sentences.zh: 改知無為軍，與光州守柴中行、安豐守陸峻俱稱循吏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Wuwei Army. Together with Chai Zhonghang, prefect of Guang Prefecture, and Lu Jun, prefect of Anfeng, he was all called a conscientious official.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administer Wuwei Army. He, Chai Zhonghang of Guang Prefecture, and Lu Jun of Anfeng were all praised as model officials.

sentences.zh: 時金人內變，有旨令獻料敵、備邊二策。

translations.literal: At that time the Jurchens were embroiled in internal turmoil, and an edict ordered the submission of two plans: one for assessing the enemy and one for border defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens were torn by internal strife, the throne ordered memorials offering two kinds of advice: how to read the enemy and how to strengthen the borders.

sentences.zh: 其料敵之策曰：“禍亂猶在河北，未遽至河南，蓋豪雄擇形勢，大盜窺貨寶，金帛重器俱聚河北，河南無大川為之險，欲起安所憑？

translations.literal: His plan for assessing the enemy said: 'Disaster and turmoil are still in Hebei and will not quickly reach Henan. Heroes choose favorable terrain; great robbers covet treasure. Gold, silk, and heavy goods are all gathered in Hebei. Henan has no great river as a barrier—if they wish to rise, upon what will they rely?'
translations.idiomatic: His assessment of the enemy read: "The chaos is still confined to Hebei and will not quickly spread to Henan. Ambitious men choose ground that favors them; bandits eye wealth. Gold, silk, and heavy goods are all concentrated in Hebei, while Henan lacks a great river for defense. If rebels mean to rise there, what would they rely on?"

sentences.zh: 且金素以河南近我，置守多完顏氏親黨，其下亦令蕃漢錯居，所以防慮備盡。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Jin have always regarded Henan as close to us and stationed there mostly Wanyan clansmen and their kin. Below them they also ordered mixed Jurchen and Han settlement, so that precautions were fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Jin have always treated Henan as territory close to Song and have posted mostly Wanyan clansmen and their allies as garrison commanders. They also require Jurchen and Han to live intermixed below them, so that their defenses are thoroughly prepared.

sentences.zh: 縱彼喪亂，守將欲叛則自叛，何至相率盡反。

translations.literal: Even if they suffer disorder, if garrison commanders wish to rebel they will rebel on their own—how could they all revolt together?
translations.idiomatic: Even if disorder breaks out among them, any garrison commander who wants to rebel will rebel on his own. Why would they all turn against the Jin at once?

sentences.zh: 然有天下者，自不容易一日廢備，豈以金人存亡之候為吾緩急哉！

translations.literal: Yet one who holds the realm should not lightly abandon preparedness for a single day. How can one make our urgency depend on whether the Jurchens live or die!
translations.idiomatic: Yet whoever holds the realm must never for a day relax its defenses. How can our own readiness depend on whether the Jurchens survive or perish!

sentences.zh: ”其備邊之策曰：“今邊州大抵無城，缺兵少糧，鎧仗不足。

translations.literal: His plan for border defense said: 'Today the border prefectures generally have no walls, lack troops and have little grain, and are short of armor and weapons.'
translations.idiomatic: His border-defense plan read: "The frontier prefectures today mostly lack walls, are short of troops and grain, and have insufficient armor and weapons."

sentences.zh: 若使自辦，何所取資？

translations.literal: If they are made to provide for themselves, from what will they draw resources?
translations.idiomatic: If they must supply themselves, where will the resources come from?

sentences.zh: 丐諸朝廷，安得力給？

translations.literal: If they beg from the court, how can it supply them fully?
translations.idiomatic: If they must beg aid from the court, how can it provide enough?

sentences.zh: 若仿古藩封，拔用英傑守郡，則並租稅市榷之利盡與之，免其共貢，上不置監臨，下悉聽選辟，民得自賦，兵得自募，凡百悉聽所為。

translations.literal: If, following the ancient enfeoffment of feudatories, outstanding men are selected to guard the prefectures, then together with them should be given all profits from land tax and market levies, exempting them from tribute to the center. Above, no overseers should be placed; below, all selection and recruitment should be left to them. The people may levy their own taxes, troops may be recruited on their own, and in all matters they should be allowed to act as they see fit.
translations.idiomatic: If, following the ancient model of enfeoffment, outstanding men were chosen to hold frontier prefectures, they should receive all revenue from land taxes and market levies, be freed from tribute to the center, and be left without supervisory officials above them. They should be allowed to choose and appoint subordinates freely, levy taxes locally, and raise troops themselves—in short, to act with full autonomy.

sentences.zh: 其有功者亦不遽徙，就峻爵秩，增異車服，給美田宅，官其子孫，凡可優寵，無不極至，使內為公卿，雖貴曾不如守邊之樂。

translations.literal: Those who achieve merit should not be quickly transferred. On the spot their ranks and titles should be raised, their carriages and robes made distinctive, fine fields and houses granted, and their sons and grandsons given office. Every possible favor should be carried to the utmost, so that even those who become ministers at court, however honored, would not find it as satisfying as guarding the border.
translations.idiomatic: Those who achieved merit should not be quickly transferred away. Their ranks should be raised on the spot, their carriages and robes made distinctive, fine estates granted, and their sons and grandsons given office. Every possible honor should be heaped upon them, so that even ministers at court, however exalted, would not enjoy life as much as guarding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 如此則有才者爭自奮勵，緩急必能出死力報上。

translations.literal: Thus talented men would compete to exert themselves, and in crisis they would surely give their lives in service to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Then men of talent would strive to excel, and in times of crisis they would surely give their lives in service to the throne.

sentences.zh: ”於後河南二十餘年猶為金守，宋沿邊諸郡權大削，兵事無肯任責者，汝談之言若蓍龜然。

translations.literal: Afterward Henan remained under Jin control for more than twenty years. Song's border prefectures saw their authority greatly reduced, and no one was willing to take responsibility for military affairs. Rutan's words proved as reliable as divination by tortoise shell.
translations.idiomatic: In the decades that followed, Henan remained under Jin control for more than twenty years, Song's frontier prefectures lost much of their authority, and no one would take responsibility for military affairs. Rutan's words proved as prescient as oracle bones.

sentences.zh: 改湖北提舉常平，振饑盡力。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Hubei and exerted himself fully in famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Hubei and threw himself wholeheartedly into famine relief.

sentences.zh: 知溫州，改知外宗正，作詩勉其族屬，皆望風而化。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Wen Prefecture, then was transferred to administer the Outer Imperial Clan Court. He composed poems to encourage his clansmen, and all were transformed at the mere report of his example.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Wen Prefecture, then was transferred to administer the Outer Imperial Clan Court. The poems he wrote to encourage his kinsmen set an example that all followed.

sentences.zh: 遷江西提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 寧宗崩，以哀痛得疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong died, he fell ill from grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong died, he fell ill from grief.

sentences.zh: 賀理宗表，力寓勸戒。

translations.literal: In his congratulatory memorial to Emperor Lizong, he strongly embedded admonition and warning.
translations.idiomatic: In his congratulatory memorial to Emperor Lizong, he strongly embedded admonition and counsel.

sentences.zh: 陳碩曰：“此諫書也。

translations.literal: Chen Shuo said: 'This is a remonstrance, not a congratulation.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuo remarked, "This is a remonstrance, not a congratulatory memorial."

sentences.zh: ”數丐祠，授江西轉運判官，辭不獲命，之官一月，以言者罷。

translations.literal: He repeatedly begged for a sinecure appointment. He was granted the post of Transport Vice Commissioner in Jiangxi. He declined but could not obtain permission to refuse. After one month in office he was dismissed because of critics.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly requested a sinecure. He was appointed Transport Vice Commissioner in Jiangxi; though he tried to decline, he could not obtain permission. After one month in office he was dismissed because of critics.

sentences.zh: 先是，汝談因疾去官，言者謂其傲睨軒冕，不樂為世用。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Rutan left office because of illness, critics said he looked down on official rank and did not wish to serve the age.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Rutan had left office because of illness, critics claimed he scorned official rank and had no wish to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 至是彌遠不與祠，乃杜門著述。

translations.literal: At this point Miyuan did not grant him a sinecure, so he shut his doors and devoted himself to writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Miyuan refused to grant him a sinecure, he shut his doors and devoted himself to writing.

sentences.zh: 端平初，以禮部郎官召，入對言：“倚用老成，廣集忠智，訪求眾敝之原，辟取可行之策，以飭積蠹之蠱，而成終泰之功者，願加聖心焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duanping era he was summoned as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites. Entering audience he said: 'To rely on seasoned men, gather loyal and wise counsel broadly, seek the root of many abuses, and adopt feasible policies in order to rectify long-standing corruption and achieve lasting peace—may Your Majesty give these matters added attention.'
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duanping era he was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites. In audience he said, "To rely on seasoned men, gather loyal and wise counsel, seek out the roots of widespread abuses, and adopt feasible policies to purge long-standing corruption and achieve lasting peace—may Your Majesty give these matters your full attention."

sentences.zh: ”又言：“大佞似忠，大奸似聖，未免信向而擢任之。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Great flatterers resemble the loyal, and great villains resemble sages. One cannot avoid trusting and promoting them.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Great flatterers can look loyal, and great villains can look sage-like. It is all too easy to trust such men and promote them."

sentences.zh: 始未見甚失，久乃浸至差訛，則綱維之臣將不能不執，議論之士將不得不言。

translations.literal: At first no great fault is seen, but in time errors gradually spread. Then ministers who uphold the framework cannot but hold firm, and men of discussion cannot but speak out.
translations.idiomatic: At first no serious fault appears, but in time errors gradually spread. Then ministers who uphold the state's framework cannot but hold firm, and critics cannot but speak out.

sentences.zh: 執之堅，寧不疑其侵權？

translations.literal: If they hold firm, will one not suspect them of encroaching on authority?
translations.idiomatic: When they hold firm, will you not suspect them of overstepping their authority?

sentences.zh: 言之數，寧不意其賣直？

translations.literal: If they speak repeatedly, will one not think they are selling righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: When they speak repeatedly, will you not think they are merely posturing as upright men?

sentences.zh: 至是則不特是非邪正易位，而黜陟予奪失中多矣。

translations.literal: At that point not only do right and wrong and good and evil change places, but dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments often miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: At that point not only do right and wrong trade places, but dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments go badly awry.

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“外之得以窒吾聽、雜吾目、擾吾天君者，以吾未得虛一而靜之理也。

translations.literal: He also said: 'That external things can block my hearing, confuse my sight, and disturb my sovereign mind is because I have not yet attained the principle of emptiness, unity, and stillness.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "External things can block my hearing, cloud my sight, and disturb my sovereign mind only because I have not yet attained the principle of emptiness, unity, and stillness."

sentences.zh: 苟得之，導我聲色而不能入，投我寶貨而不能中，扇我以功名而不能動，凝然湛然，孰得幹之哉。

translations.literal: If one attains it, though music and beauty lead one they cannot enter; though treasure is cast at one it cannot strike home; though fame and merit fan one they cannot move one. Serene and deep, who could interfere?
translations.idiomatic: Once one attains it, music and beauty may lead one but cannot penetrate; treasure may be offered but cannot reach one; fame and glory may be waved before one but cannot move one. Serene and deep within, who could disturb such a mind?

sentences.zh: ”改秘書少監兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently given acting duty in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent acting duty in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時集議出師，汝談反覆言不可輕戰，而和尤非計。

translations.literal: At that time the court assembled to discuss dispatching troops. Rutan repeatedly said war must not be lightly undertaken, and that peace was an especially poor plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the court assembled to debate sending troops abroad, Rutan repeatedly argued that war must not be lightly undertaken and that seeking peace was an especially poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 既而三京收復，雖前言用兵不便者亦喜，汝談獨有憂色。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Three Capitals were recovered. Even those who had earlier said war was inadvisable rejoiced, but Rutan alone wore a look of worry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Capitals were soon recovered, even those who had earlier opposed war rejoiced, but Rutan alone looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，洛師敗，朝論始服其先見。

translations.literal: Before long the Luoyang army was defeated, and court opinion at last acknowledged his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the army at Luoyang was defeated, and the court at last acknowledged his foresight.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正少卿，兼權直，兼編修國史、檢討實錄，兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, concurrently acting Hanlin duty, concurrently Compiler of the National History and Examiner of the Veritable Records, and concurrently Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, with concurrent acting Hanlin duty, concurrent posts as Compiler of the National History and Examiner of the Veritable Records, and concurrent appointment as Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 因講《論語》而言漢元帝恭儉無過，惟以剛不克改，明不能繹，優柔不斷，而漢業遂衰。

translations.literal: While lecturing on the Analects he spoke of Emperor Yuan of Han, saying that though reverent and frugal he was without fault, yet because he lacked firmness to reform, clarity to follow through, and resolve to decide, the Han enterprise declined.
translations.idiomatic: While lecturing on the Analects he observed that Emperor Yuan of Han, though reverent and frugal and without personal fault, lacked the firmness to reform, the clarity to follow through, and the resolve to decide—and so the Han dynasty declined.

sentences.zh: 權吏部侍郎，升侍讀，兼直學士院，兼同修國史院同修撰，以所注《易》進講。

translations.literal: He was given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Personnel, promoted to Court Reader, concurrently given Hanlin duty, concurrently made Associate Compiler of the National History Institute, and presented his commentary on the Changes for imperial lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Vice Minister of Personnel, was promoted to Court Reader, held concurrent Hanlin duty and an associate compilership in the National History Institute, and presented his commentary on the Changes for imperial lecture.

sentences.zh: 時朝議履畝稱楮，汝談言非便，迕時宰意。

translations.literal: At that time the court debated surveying fields to value paper currency. Rutan said it was not expedient and offended the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated surveying fields to support the paper currency, Rutan argued that the policy was ill-advised and offended the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 京師軍變，宰相乞貶秩，上已允，汝談奏恐失體，持不可。

translations.literal: When the capital garrison mutinied, the chief minister begged to be demoted in rank. The emperor had already agreed, but Rutan memorialized that this would damage dignity and firmly objected.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital garrison mutinied, the chief minister asked to be demoted in rank. The emperor had already agreed, but Rutan memorialized that this would damage the dignity of the office and firmly objected.

sentences.zh: 草答詔，以為貶秩易，審舉措難，宰相滋不悅。

translations.literal: Drafting the reply edict, he held that demotion in rank was easy but careful action was difficult. The chief minister grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In drafting the reply edict he argued that demotion was easy but sound action was difficult. The chief minister grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 以言去國，提舉崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He left the court because of his words and was made superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because of his outspokenness and appointed superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知婺州，四辭不允。

translations.literal: He was recalled to govern Wu Prefecture. He declined four times but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Wu Prefecture. He declined four times but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 至郡，力丐祠。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture, he forcefully begged for a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the prefecture, he urgently requested a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在，四辭。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the temporary capital and declined four times.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the temporary capital and declined four times.

sentences.zh: 權禮部侍郎兼學士院，力辭兼直。

translations.literal: He was given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent Hanlin duty and forcefully declined the concurrent Hanlin post.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent Hanlin duty and firmly declined the concurrent Hanlin appointment.

sentences.zh: 時金兵新破，三閫增秩，稱提官楮，四郡獲賞。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin army had just been defeated. The three commanders were promoted in rank, currency commissioners raised the value of paper notes, and four prefectures received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army had just been defeated. The three frontier commanders were promoted, currency commissioners raised the value of paper notes, and four prefectures received rewards.

sentences.zh: 汝談獨蹙頞，登對，首疏言：“邊麵無可倚仗，乞超越拘攣，簡拔俊傑，如吳用周瑜、魯肅，晉任祖逖、陶侃故事，使之各分方麵，連數十城，推轂授權，盡歸賜履。

translations.literal: Rutan alone furrowed his brow. Entering audience, his first memorial said: 'The frontier has nothing to rely on. I beg that constraints be transcended and outstanding men selected, following the precedents of Wu employing Zhou Yu and Lu Su, and Jin appointing Zu Ti and Tao Kan, so that each may hold a separate sector, linking dozens of cities, with full authority granted and complete discretionary power given.'
translations.idiomatic: Rutan alone furrowed his brow. In audience his opening memorial read: "The frontier has nothing we can rely on. I beg that normal constraints be set aside and outstanding men chosen, following the precedents of Wu employing Zhou Yu and Lu Su and Jin appointing Zu Ti and Tao Kan, so that each may hold a separate sector linking dozens of cities, with full authority granted and complete discretionary power."

sentences.zh: 巴蜀一人，荊襄一人，兩淮各一人，一切便宜行事，不復更從中禦，庶幾伸縮由己，機用出心。

translations.literal: One man for Ba-Shu, one for Jing-Xiang, one each for the two Huai regions—all to act at discretion in all matters and no longer receive orders from the center, so that expansion and contraction depend on themselves and strategy comes from their own minds.
translations.idiomatic: One man for Ba-Shu, one for Jing-Xiang, and one each for the two Huai regions—all to act at full discretion without further orders from the center, so that they may expand or contract as they see fit and devise strategy from their own judgment.

sentences.zh: ”蓋推廣向者備邊之策。

translations.literal: This was essentially an extension of his earlier plan for border defense.
translations.idiomatic: This was essentially an extension of his earlier border-defense plan.

sentences.zh: 且曰：“臣之此策，行於開禧未用兵之前，決不至罹今日之患。

translations.literal: He also said: 'If my plan had been carried out before the Kaixi campaign, before troops were sent, we would certainly not have suffered today's calamity.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "If this plan of mine had been adopted before the Kaixi campaign, before troops were sent, we would never have suffered today's disaster."

sentences.zh: ”其論楮法，尤中時敝，上稱歎久之，且謂：“卿文學高世，宜代予言，力辭何為？

translations.literal: His discussion of paper currency especially hit the abuses of the time. The emperor praised him at length and also said: 'Your literary learning surpasses the age. You ought to speak for me—why forcefully decline?'
translations.idiomatic: His analysis of paper currency especially struck at the abuses of the day. The emperor praised him at length and said, "Your learning surpasses your age. You ought to speak for me—why keep declining?"

sentences.zh: ”卒以老祈免，章四上，免兼直，改侍講。

translations.literal: In the end he begged exemption on grounds of age. After four memorials he was relieved of concurrent Hanlin duty and transferred to Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he requested exemption on grounds of age. After four memorials he was relieved of concurrent Hanlin duty and transferred to Court Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 數日，仍兼直學士院，五辭。

translations.literal: Several days later he was again given concurrent Hanlin duty and declined five times.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was again given concurrent Hanlin duty and declined five times.

sentences.zh: 權給事中，權刑部尚書，及卒，轉兩官。

translations.literal: He served as acting Supervising Secretary and acting Minister of Justice. Upon his death two ranks were posthumously conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Supervising Secretary and acting Minister of Justice. Upon his death two ranks were posthumously conferred.

sentences.zh: 遺表上，又轉四官。

translations.literal: When his death memorial was submitted, four more ranks were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial was submitted, four more ranks were posthumously conferred.

sentences.zh: 汝談天資絕人，沈思高識，自少至老，無一日去書冊。

translations.literal: Rutan's natural endowment surpassed others. His deep thought and lofty insight never left books for a single day from youth to old age.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan's natural gifts surpassed those of ordinary men. Deep in thought and lofty in insight, he never spent a day without books from youth to old age.

sentences.zh: 其論《易》，以為為占者作；

translations.literal: In his discussion of the Changes, he held that it was written for diviners;
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the Changes, he held that it was written for diviners;

sentences.zh: 書《堯》、《舜》二典宜合為一，禹功隻施於河洛，《洪範》非箕子之作；

translations.literal: in the Documents, the two canons of Yao and Shun should be combined into one; Yu's achievements apply only to the Yellow River and Luo regions; the Great Plan was not written by Jizi;
translations.idiomatic: in the Documents, the two canons of Yao and Shun should be combined into one; Yu's achievements apply only to the Yellow River and Luo regions; the Great Plan was not written by Jizi;

sentences.zh: 《詩》不以《小序》為信；

translations.literal: in the Odes, the Small Prefaces should not be trusted;
translations.idiomatic: in the Odes, the Small Prefaces should not be trusted;

sentences.zh: 《禮記》雜出諸生之手；

translations.literal: the Record of Rites was mixed together from the hands of various scholars;
translations.idiomatic: the Record of Rites was compiled from the work of various scholars;

sentences.zh: 《周禮》宜傅會女主之書。

translations.literal: the Rites of Zhou should be regarded as a book forced together to suit a female ruler.
translations.idiomatic: the Rites of Zhou was likely stitched together to suit a female ruler.

sentences.zh: 要亦卓絕特立之見。

translations.literal: In sum these were also views outstanding and standing apart.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, these were bold and unconventional views.

sentences.zh: 為文章有天巧。

translations.literal: In composing essays he had heaven's skill.
translations.idiomatic: His prose possessed an almost effortless brilliance.

sentences.zh: 篤於倫誼而忘仇怨，御史王益祥嚐劾之，後汝談官其鄉，益祥愧不敢見，汝談乃數過之，相得歡甚。

translations.literal: He was devoted to human bonds and forgot enmity. Censor Wang Yixiang had once impeached him. Later, when Rutan served in Yixiang's home district, Yixiang was ashamed and dared not see him. Rutan then visited him several times, and they got on extremely well.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to human bonds and forgot old grudges. Censor Wang Yixiang had once impeached him. Later, when Rutan held office in Yixiang's home district, Yixiang was ashamed and dared not visit him. Rutan sought him out several times, and they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 嚐論議韓非、李斯皆有荀卿之才，惟其富貴利欲之心重，故世得而賤之，惟卿獨能守其身，不苟希合，士何可不自重哉。

translations.literal: He once observed that Han Fei and Li Si both had the talent of Xun Qing, but because their hearts were heavy with desire for wealth and profit, the age could despise them. Only Qing was able to keep himself intact and not casually seek approval. How could a gentleman fail to respect himself!
translations.idiomatic: He once observed that Han Fei and Li Si both had the talent of Xun Qing, but because they were consumed by desire for wealth and power, the world despised them. Only Xun Qing kept himself intact and refused to curry favor. How could a gentleman fail to hold himself in esteem!

sentences.zh: 所著有《易》、《書》、《詩》、《論語》、《孟子》、《周禮》、《禮記》、《荀子》、《莊子》、《通鑒》、《杜詩注》。

translations.literal: His written works include commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Analects, Mencius, Rites of Zhou, Record of Rites, Xunzi, Zhuangzi, Comprehensive Mirror, and Du Fu's poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His written works include commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Analects, Mencius, Rites of Zhou, Record of Rites, Xunzi, Zhuangzi, the Comprehensive Mirror, and Du Fu's poetry.

sentences.zh: 趙汝讜，字蹈中，少俶儻有軼材，智略出人上。

translations.literal: Zhao Rudang, styled Daozhong, in youth was unconventional and had extraordinary talent; his wisdom and strategy surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rudang, courtesy name Daozhong, was unconventional in youth and possessed extraordinary talent; his wisdom and strategic insight surpassed those around him.

sentences.zh: 龍泉葉適嚐過其家，汝讜年少，衣短後衣，不得避。

translations.literal: Ye Shi of Longquan once visited his home. Rudang was young and wore short riding clothes, and could not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Shi of Longquan once visited his home. Rudang was still young and wore short riding clothes, and could not withdraw to change.

sentences.zh: 適勸之曰：“名門子安可不學。

translations.literal: Shi admonished him, saying: 'How can the son of a distinguished family fail to study?'
translations.idiomatic: Ye Shi admonished him, saying, "How can the son of a distinguished family fail to study?"

sentences.zh: ”汝讜慚，自是終身不衣短後衣。

translations.literal: Rudang was ashamed, and from then on never wore short riding clothes for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Rudang was ashamed, and from that day forward he never wore short riding clothes again.

sentences.zh: 折節讀書，與兄汝談齊名，天下稱為“二趙”。

translations.literal: He restrained himself to study books and became as famous as his elder brother Rutan. The realm called them 'the Two Zhaos.'
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to study and became as renowned as his elder brother Rutan. The realm called them "the Two Zhaos."

sentences.zh: 以祖遺恩補承務郎，曆泉州市舶務、利州大軍倉屬。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's legacy favor he was granted the office of Chengwu Lang. He served successively at the Quanzhou Maritime Trade Office and as clerk of the Great Army Granary in Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather's privilege he received the rank of Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement. He served at the Quanzhou Maritime Trade Office and as clerk of the Great Army Granary in Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 從臣薦宗室之賢者，監行在右藏西庫。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of attendant ministers for worthy members of the imperial clan, he was made supervisor of the Western Treasury of the Right Storehouse at the temporary capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of attendant ministers for worthy members of the imperial clan, he was appointed supervisor of the Western Treasury of the Right Storehouse at the temporary capital.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄謀逐趙汝愚，汝讜兄弟昌言非是，且上言訟汝愚冤。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou plotted to expel Zhao Ruyu. The Rudang brothers spoke openly that this was wrong and also submitted memorials pleading Ruyu's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou plotted to drive Zhao Ruyu from court, the Rudang brothers spoke out against it and submitted memorials pleading Ruyu's innocence.

sentences.zh: 侂胄懼其詞直，使其黨胡紘再攻汝愚，以汝讜兄弟受汝愚厚恩，私屬為之畫策，惑亂天聽為言，斥使去國。

translations.literal: Tuozhou feared their blunt words and had his partisan Hu Hong attack Ruyu again, alleging that the Rudang brothers had received great favor from Ruyu and secretly plotted on his behalf, confusing the emperor's judgment, and had them expelled from court.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou feared their blunt speech and had his partisan Hu Hong attack Ruyu again, claiming that the Rudang brothers, having received great favor from Ruyu, had secretly plotted on his behalf and misled the emperor—and had them driven from court.

sentences.zh: 坐廢十年，調華亭浦東鹽場，棄職去。

translations.literal: He was demoted for ten years, was transferred to the Huating Pudong Salt Field, and abandoned his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted for ten years, was posted to the Huating Pudong Salt Field, and resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 辟浙西安撫司幕官，調簽書昭慶軍節度判官，皆不赴。

translations.literal: He was invited as a staff officer of the Zhexi Pacification Commission and transferred as signing secretary and military prefectural judge of Zhaoging Army, but did not take up either post.
translations.idiomatic: He was invited to serve on the staff of the Zhexi Pacification Commission and was transferred as signing secretary and military prefectural judge of Zhaoging Army, but declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 以前官改鎮東軍。

translations.literal: On the basis of his former office he was transferred to Zhendong Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the basis of his former rank he was transferred to Zhendong Army.

sentences.zh: 登嘉定元年進士第，為太社令，遷將作監簿、大理司農丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Jiading, served as Director of the Grand Altar of Earth, and was promoted to Registrar of the Directorate of Works and Assistant Director of Agriculture in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the first year of the Jiading reign (1208), served as Director of the Grand Altar of Earth, and was promoted to Registrar of the Directorate of Works and Assistant Director of Agriculture in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 與史彌遠不合，請外，改湖南提舉常平，易江西，尋提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He did not get along with Shi Miyuan and requested an outside appointment. He was transferred to Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Hunan, then exchanged to Jiangxi, and soon became Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Shi Miyuan and requested an outside appointment. He was transferred to Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Hunan, then to Jiangxi, and soon became Judicial Intendant.

sentences.zh: 瑞州大姓幸氏貪徐氏田不可得，強取其禾，終不與，誣以殺婢，置徐獄。

translations.literal: In Rui Prefecture the great clan Xing coveted the Xu family's fields but could not obtain them. They forcibly took their grain and ultimately would not return it. They falsely accused the Xus of killing a maidservant and imprisoned Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In Rui Prefecture the powerful Xing clan coveted the Xu family's land but could not obtain it. They forcibly harvested the Xus' grain and refused to return it, then falsely accused the Xus of killing a maidservant and had Xu thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 徐訴其冤，汝讜以反坐法黥竄幸氏，籍其家。

translations.literal: Xu pleaded his innocence. Rudang, applying the law of counter-charge, tattooed and banished the Xing clan and confiscated their property.
translations.idiomatic: Xu appealed his innocence. Rudang, applying the law of counter-charge, had the Xing clan tattooed and banished and confiscated their property.

sentences.zh: 幸氏走，告急於中宮，徙汝讜湖南。

translations.literal: The Xing clan fled and reported the emergency to the empress. Rudang was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The Xing clan fled and appealed to the empress. Rudang was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 既至，則表直臣龔墓。

translations.literal: Upon arriving, he submitted a memorial honoring the upright minister Gong Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arriving, he submitted a memorial honoring the upright minister Gong Mu.

sentences.zh: 瀏陽有豪民羅氏奪民田，汝讜復懲以法。

translations.literal: In Liuyang a powerful man of the Luo clan seized the people's fields. Rudang again punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In Liuyang a powerful man of the Luo clan seized commoners' land. Rudang again punished him according to law.

sentences.zh: 遷知溫州，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Wen Prefecture and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Wen Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 汝讜常言：“宗子不忘君，孝子不辱身，臨難則功業當如朱虛，立身當如子政。

translations.literal: Rudang often said: 'A clansman of the imperial house must not forget his sovereign; a filial son must not disgrace himself. In facing danger one's achievements should be like Zhu Xu, and one's conduct like Zizheng.'
translations.idiomatic: Rudang often said, "A member of the imperial clan must not forget his sovereign; a filial son must not disgrace himself. In facing danger one's achievements should be like Zhu Xu, and one's conduct like Zizheng."

sentences.zh: 趙希錧，字君錫，舊名希哲，登慶元二年進士第，改賜今名。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiguan, styled Junxi, formerly named Xizhe, passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Qingyuan and was granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiguan, courtesy name Junxi, formerly named Xizhe, passed the jinshi examinations in the second year of the Qingyuan reign (1196) and was granted his present name.

sentences.zh: 少扶父喪歸，道遇寇，左右駭散，希錧拊棺慟哭不懾，寇義而去。

translations.literal: In youth, while escorting his father's coffin home, he encountered bandits on the road. His attendants fled in terror, but Xiguan beat the coffin and wept without fear. The bandits, moved by righteousness, departed.
translations.idiomatic: While still young, escorting his father's coffin home, he encountered bandits on the road. His attendants fled in terror, but Xiguan beat the coffin and wept without flinching. The bandits, moved by his conduct, let him pass.

sentences.zh: 學於陳傅良、徐誼，既舉進士，調汀州司戶。

translations.literal: He studied under Chen Fuliang and Xu Yi. After passing the jinshi examination he was assigned as Revenue Recorder of Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Chen Fuliang and Xu Yi. After passing the jinshi examinations he was assigned as Revenue Recorder of Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 峒寇李元礪方起，汀人震懼，郡會僚佐議守城，希錧下坐無一語，守異之曰：“不言得無有所見乎？

translations.literal: The cave-bandit Li Yuanli had just risen in revolt. The people of Ting were shaken with fear. At a prefectural meeting the staff discussed defending the city. Xiguan, seated below, said not a word. The prefect, finding this strange, said: 'By saying nothing, do you perhaps have some view?'
translations.idiomatic: The cave-bandit Li Yuanli had just risen in revolt, and the people of Ting were terrified. At a prefectural meeting the staff debated defending the city. Xiguan, seated below, said nothing. The prefect, puzzled, asked, "By saying nothing, do you perhaps have some view?"

sentences.zh: ”希錧曰：“守城非策也，距城三十里有關曰古城，若悉精銳以扼其衝，賊不足慮矣。

translations.literal: Xiguan said: 'Defending the city is not the strategy. Thirty li from the city there is a pass called Gucheng. If all elite troops are sent to hold its choke point, the bandits need not be feared.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiguan replied, "Defending the city is not the right strategy. Thirty li from the city there is a pass called Gucheng. If we send all our best troops to hold that choke point, the bandits need not be feared."

sentences.zh: ”守以付希錧，人為危之。

translations.literal: The prefect entrusted the matter to Xiguan, and people regarded it as dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect entrusted the matter to Xiguan, and many thought it perilous.

sentences.zh: 希錧至關，審形明間，申令謹候，分畫粗定，賊已遣諜窺關。

translations.literal: Xiguan reached the pass, examined the terrain and identified the gaps, issued strict orders for vigilance, and roughly divided the dispositions. The bandits had already sent spies to reconnoiter the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguan reached the pass, surveyed the terrain and identified the weak points, issued strict orders for vigilance, and roughly set the dispositions. The bandits had already sent spies to scout the pass.

sentences.zh: 希錧得諜詰之，縱其舉火相示，而羸師以誤之。

translations.literal: Xiguan captured a spy and interrogated him, then released him to signal by fire, while displaying a weakened force to deceive the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguan captured a spy and interrogated him, then released him to signal by fire while displaying a weakened force to deceive the enemy.

sentences.zh: 夜半，賊數百銜枚突至，希錧嚴兵以待。

translations.literal: At midnight several hundred bandits arrived silently with gags in their mouths. Xiguan held his troops in strict readiness.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight several hundred bandits arrived silently with gags in their mouths. Xiguan held his troops in strict readiness.

sentences.zh: 賊且至，始命矢石俱下，賊無一免，餘黨聞風而遁。

translations.literal: As the bandits were about to arrive, he at last ordered arrows and stones to rain down together. Not one bandit escaped, and the remaining followers fled at the news.
translations.idiomatic: As the bandits drew near, he at last ordered arrows and stones to rain down together. Not one escaped, and the remaining followers fled at the news.

sentences.zh: 希錧引還，老稚羅拜相屬，希錧繇他道以避之。

translations.literal: Xiguan led his troops back. Old and young lined up to bow in succession. Xiguan took another road to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguan led his troops back. Old and young lined the road to bow in gratitude. Xiguan took another route to avoid the crowd.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔升州推官，治疑獄，決滯訟，攝下邑，弭亂卒。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict promoted him to Prefectural Investigating Officer. He resolved doubtful cases, decided stalled lawsuits, acted in place of subordinate counties, and quelled mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict promoted him to Prefectural Investigating Officer. He resolved doubtful cases, cleared stalled lawsuits, administered subordinate counties, and quelled mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 去之日，軍民遮道泣送者數十里。

translations.literal: On the day he departed, soldiers and civilians blocked the road weeping and escorting him for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he departed, soldiers and civilians blocked the road weeping and escorted him for miles.

sentences.zh: 調主管夔州路轉運司帳司，疏大寧鹽井利病，使者上諸朝，民便之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to manage the accounts office of the Kuizhou Circuit Transport Commission. He memorialized on the benefits and harms of the Daning salt wells. The commissioner forwarded it to court, and the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to manage the accounts office of the Kuizhou Circuit Transport Commission. He memorialized on the benefits and harms of the Daning salt wells. The commissioner forwarded it to court, and the people benefited.

sentences.zh: 改知玉山縣，未行。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Yushan County but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administer Yushan County but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 召對，希錧首言民力困於貪吏，軍力困於僨帥，國家之力則外困於歸附之卒，內困於浮冗之費；

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, Xiguan first spoke of the people's strength exhausted by corrupt officials, military strength exhausted by arrogant commanders, and the state's strength externally exhausted by surrendered troops and internally exhausted by wasteful expenditures;
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, Xiguan first spoke of the people's strength exhausted by corrupt officials, military strength exhausted by arrogant commanders, and the state's strength externally drained by surrendered troops and internally drained by wasteful expenditures;

sentences.zh: 次論四蜀銓科舉之弊；

translations.literal: next he discussed the abuses of examinations and selection in the Four Shu regions;
translations.idiomatic: next he discussed the abuses of examinations and official selection in the Four Shu regions;

sentences.zh: 次論大寧鹽井本末。

translations.literal: next he discussed the full history of the Daning salt wells.
translations.idiomatic: and finally he discussed the full history of the Daning salt wells.

sentences.zh: 寧宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ningzong praised and accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ningzong praised and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 授大理寺丞，遷大宗正丞，權工部郎官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and given acting appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and given acting appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 宗姓多貧，而始生有訓名，為人後有過禮，吏受賕亡藝，莫敢自陳，希錧白其長推行之。

translations.literal: Many of the imperial clan were poor, yet newborn children had instruction names, adoption involved excessive ritual, and clerks accepted bribes beyond their proper fees, yet none dared speak out. Xiguan reported this to his superior and had reforms carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Many members of the imperial clan were poor, yet newborn children were given instruction names, adoption involved excessive ritual, and clerks accepted improper bribes, yet none dared speak out. Xiguan reported this to his superior and had reforms carried out.

sentences.zh: 會朝議，燕邸近屬赴朝參者少，命希錧易班，希錧力辭，弗克。

translations.literal: At a court discussion it was noted that few close relatives of the Prince of Yan attended court audiences. Xiguan was ordered to change ranks. He forcefully declined but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At court it was noted that few close relatives of the Prince of Yan attended audiences. Xiguan was ordered to change ranks. He firmly declined but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 特換授吉州刺史、提舉佑神觀。

translations.literal: He was specially transferred and appointed Prefect of Ji Prefecture and Superintendent of the Youshen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially transferred and appointed Prefect of Ji Prefecture and Superintendent of the Youshen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廷臣言宗姓換班人嚐舉進士，請視朝士，聽輪對。

translations.literal: Before long court ministers said that those of the imperial clan who changed ranks had once passed the jinshi examination and requested that they be treated like court officials and allowed rotating audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Before long court ministers noted that members of the imperial clan who changed ranks had passed the jinshi examinations and requested that they be treated like court officials and allowed rotating audiences.

sentences.zh: 於是希錧次對時首論：“今日多事之際，而未有辦事之人。

translations.literal: Thereupon, at his next audience Xiguan first observed: 'In today's time of many affairs, there are no men who can get things done.'
translations.idiomatic: At his next audience Xiguan opened by saying, "In these troubled times, there are no men who can actually get things done."

sentences.zh: 朝紳，清選也，以緘默為清重，以刻薄為舉職，以無所可否為識體。

translations.literal: Court officials are a pure selection, yet silence is taken as dignified restraint, harshness as fulfilling duty, and having no yes or no as understanding propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials are supposed to be the best of men, yet silence is taken for dignified restraint, harshness for fulfilling duty, and having no opinion for understanding propriety.

sentences.zh: 閫寄，重任也，以大言為有誌，以使過為知恩。

translations.literal: Frontier command is a weighty responsibility, yet grand talk is taken as having ambition, and covering faults as knowing gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier command is a weighty responsibility, yet grand talk is taken for ambition, and covering up faults for gratitude.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢厚誣天下以為無人，患在選擇未得其道、器使未當其才爾。

translations.literal: Your servant does not dare greatly slander the realm as having no men. The trouble lies in selection not finding the right path and deployment not matching talent.
translations.idiomatic: I do not mean to slander the realm as having no capable men. The trouble lies in selection not finding the right path and deployment not matching talent.

sentences.zh: ”授成州團練使，賜金帶，令服係。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Cheng Prefecture, granted a gold belt, and ordered to wear it in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Cheng Prefecture, granted a gold belt, and ordered to wear it in office.

sentences.zh: 以寶璽推恩，進和州防禦使。

translations.literal: Through the imperial seal's extension of favor he was promoted to Defender-in-Chief of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through the imperial seal's extension of favor he was promoted to Defender-in-Chief of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 希錧風資凝重，胸抱魁壘，揚人之善，不記人之過，急人之難，不忘人之恩。

translations.literal: Xiguan's bearing was dignified and grave. His breast held great substance. He praised others' virtues, did not remember others' faults, hastened to others' difficulties, and did not forget others' kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguan's bearing was dignified and grave, and his mind held great substance. He praised others' virtues and forgot their faults, hastened to their difficulties and remembered their kindness.

sentences.zh: 居官，祁寒盛暑未嚐謁告，衣食取裁足而已。

translations.literal: In office, through bitter cold and blazing heat he never once requested leave. For food and clothing he took only what sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: In office, through bitter cold and blazing heat he never once requested leave. For food and clothing he took only what sufficed.

sentences.zh: 追封信安郡王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xinan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xinan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 趙彥呐，字敏若，彭州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanne, styled Minruo, was a native of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanne, courtesy name Minruo, was a native of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登四川類試第。

translations.literal: He passed the Sichuan regional examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Sichuan regional examination.

sentences.zh: 少以材稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was known for his talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for his talent.

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，以祿禧偽守夔，彥呐結義士殺之，遂顯名。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled, Lu Xi was made false prefect of Kui. Yanne gathered righteous men and killed him, and thereby gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, Lu Xi was installed as puppet prefect of Kui. Yanne gathered loyal men and killed him, and thereby gained renown.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十二年，關外西和州新被兵，製使安丙檄使經理，金人再至，戰卻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiading, Xihe Prefecture beyond the passes had newly suffered attack. Commissioner An Bing ordered Yanne to manage affairs there. The Jurchens came again and he fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Jiading reign (1219), Xihe Prefecture beyond the passes had newly suffered attack. Commissioner An Bing ordered Yanne to manage affairs there. The Jurchens came again and he fought them off.

sentences.zh: 因請修州北水關，募民耕戰以守；

translations.literal: He therefore requested repair of the water pass north of the prefecture and recruitment of civilians to farm and fight in defense;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore requested repair of the water pass north of the prefecture and recruitment of civilians to farm and fight in defense;

sentences.zh: 又勸丙盡捐關外四州租，結民兵使各自為守。

translations.literal: he also urged Bing to completely remit the land tax of the four prefectures beyond the passes and organize local militia so each area could defend itself.
translations.idiomatic: he also urged Bing to remit entirely the land tax of the four prefectures beyond the passes and organize local militia so each area could defend itself.

sentences.zh: 皆不行。

translations.literal: None of these proposals was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: None of these proposals was adopted.

sentences.zh: 在州五年，得軍民心，轉提點刑獄，尋帥沔，時譽甚都。

translations.literal: He remained in the prefecture five years and won the hearts of soldiers and civilians. He was transferred to Judicial Intendant and soon commanded Mian. His contemporary reputation was very high.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in the prefecture five years and won the hearts of soldiers and civilians. He was transferred to Judicial Intendant and soon commanded Mian. His contemporary reputation was very high.

sentences.zh: 及崔與之代丙，始察其大言無實，謂他日誤事省必此人，請廟堂毋付以邊藩。

translations.literal: When Cui Yuzhi replaced Bing, he at last perceived that Yanne's grand talk had no substance. He said that when affairs went wrong in the future this man would surely be the cause, and requested the court not to entrust him with a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuzhi replaced Bing, he at last saw that Yanne's grand talk had no substance. He said that when affairs went wrong this man would surely be the cause, and asked the court not to entrust him with a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 尋奪其節製。

translations.literal: Soon his military commission was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his military commission was revoked.

sentences.zh: 趙善湘字清臣，濮安懿王五世孫。

translations.literal: Zhao Shanxiang, styled Qingchen, was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Pu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shanxiang, courtesy name Qingchen, was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Pu'an.

sentences.zh: 父武翼郎不陋，從高宗渡江，聞明州多名儒，徙居焉。

translations.literal: His father Bulou, a Military Guard Officer, followed Emperor Gaozong across the Yangzi. Hearing that Ming Prefecture had many eminent scholars, he moved there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bulou, a Military Guard Officer, followed Emperor Gaozong across the Yangzi. Hearing that Ming Prefecture had many eminent scholars, he moved there.

sentences.zh: 善湘以恩補保義郎，轉成忠郎、監潭州南嶽廟，轉忠翊郎，又轉忠訓郎。

translations.literal: Shanxiang, through privilege, was granted the office of Baoyi Lang. He was transferred to Chenzhong Lang and made Superintendent of the Southern Peak Temple in Tan Prefecture, then transferred to Zhongyi Lang and again to Zhongxun Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxiang, through privilege, received the rank of Gentleman for Righteous Service. He was transferred to Gentleman for Loyalty, made Superintendent of the Southern Peak Temple in Tan Prefecture, then promoted to Gentleman for Assisting Loyalty and again to Gentleman for Instructing Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年舉進士，以近屬轉秉義郎，換承事郎，調金壇縣丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan he passed the jinshi examination. As a close imperial relative he was transferred to Bingyi Lang, exchanged to Chengshi Lang, and assigned as Assistant Magistrate of Jintan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Qingyuan reign (1196) he passed the jinshi examinations. As a close imperial relative he was transferred to Gentleman for Upholding Righteousness, exchanged to Gentleman for Meritorious Service, and assigned as Assistant Magistrate of Jintan County.

sentences.zh: 五年，知餘姚縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he governed Yuyao County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he governed Yuyao County.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，添差通判婺州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi he was given an additional appointment as vice prefect of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Kaixi reign (1205) he received a supplementary appointment as vice prefect of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，以招茶寇功，赴都堂審察，提轄文思院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading, for merit in recruiting tea bandits, he underwent review at the chief council and was made Administrator of the Wensi Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jiading reign (1208), for merit in recruiting tea bandits, he underwent review at the chief council and was made Administrator of the Wensi Institute.

sentences.zh: 出判無為軍兼淮南轉運判官、淮西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefectural judge of Wuwei Army, concurrently Transport Vice Commissioner of Huainan and Judicial Intendant of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefectural judge of Wuwei Army, concurrently Transport Vice Commissioner of Huainan and Judicial Intendant of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 四年，改知常州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to govern Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to govern Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，主管武夷山衝佑觀。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made superintendent of the Chongyou Abbey on Mount Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made superintendent of the Chongyou Abbey on Mount Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 十年，知湖州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he governed Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he governed Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丁內艱，明年起復，知和州，三辭不獲命。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he completed mourning for his mother. The next year he was recalled from mourning to govern He Prefecture. He declined three times but could not obtain permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he completed mourning for his mother. The next year he was recalled from mourning to govern He Prefecture. He declined three times but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 遷知大宗正丞兼權戶部郎官，改知秘閣、淮南轉運判官，兼淮西提舉常平，兼知無為軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent acting appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, transferred to Library Director and Transport Vice Commissioner of Huainan, concurrently Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Huai West, and concurrently administrator of Wuwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent acting appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, transferred to Library Director and Transport Vice Commissioner of Huainan, concurrently Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Huai West, and concurrently administrator of Wuwei Army.

sentences.zh: 進直徽猷閣、主管淮南製置司公事，兼知廬州，兼本路安撫，仍兼轉運判官、提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Huiyou Pavilion, placed in charge of the Huainan Military Commission, concurrently governing Lu Prefecture, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of the circuit, and still concurrently Transport Vice Commissioner and Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Huiyou Pavilion, placed in charge of the Huainan Military Commission, concurrently governing Lu Prefecture, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of the circuit, and still concurrently Transport Vice Commissioner and Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進直寶文閣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 以平固始寇功，賜金帶，許令服係。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing bandits in Gushi he was granted a gold belt and permitted to wear it in office.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in suppressing bandits in Gushi he was granted a gold belt and permitted to wear it in office.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進直龍圖閣、知鎮江府。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion and governed Zhenjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion and appointed prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 十七年，拜大理少卿，進右文殿修撰、知鎮江府，封祥符縣男，賜食邑。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to Compiler of the Youwen Hall and prefect of Zhenjiang, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangfu County, and granted a fief for sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to Compiler of the Youwen Hall and prefect of Zhenjiang, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangfu County, and granted a fief for sustenance.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年，進集英殿修撰，拜大理卿兼權刑部侍郎，進寶章閣待制、沿海製置使兼知建康府、江東安撫使兼主管行宮留守司公事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoqing he was promoted to Compiler of the Jiying Hall, appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review with concurrent acting appointment as Vice Minister of Justice, and promoted to Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, Coastal Military Commissioner, concurrently prefect of Jiankang, Pacification Commissioner of Jiang East, and concurrently in charge of the Temporary Palace Garrison Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Baoqing reign (1226) he was promoted to Compiler of the Jiying Hall, appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review with concurrent acting appointment as Vice Minister of Justice, and promoted to Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, Coastal Military Commissioner, concurrently prefect of Jiankang, Pacification Commissioner of Jiang East, and concurrently in charge of the Temporary Palace Garrison Commission.

sentences.zh: 賜仙花金帶，進封子，加食邑。

translations.literal: He was granted a gold belt with immortal-flower ornament, his son was advanced in rank, and his fief for sustenance was increased.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a gold belt with immortal-flower ornament, his son was advanced in rank, and his fief for sustenance was increased.

sentences.zh: 時善湘見範、葵進取，慰藉殷勤，饋問接踵，有請必應。

translations.literal: At that time Shanxiang saw Fan and Kui advancing aggressively. He consoled them warmly, sent gifts in succession, and responded to every request.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shanxiang saw Fan and Kui advancing aggressively. He consoled them warmly, sent gifts in succession, and responded to every request.

sentences.zh: 遣諸子屯寶應以從，範、葵亦讓功督府，凡得捷，皆汝櫄等握筆草報。

translations.literal: He sent his sons to camp at Baoying to follow them. Fan and Kui also yielded credit to the supervisory headquarters. Whenever victory was won, Ru Chao and the others held the brush to draft the reports.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his sons to camp at Baoying to support them. Fan and Kui also yielded credit to the supervisory headquarters. Whenever victory was won, Ru Chao and the others drafted the reports.

sentences.zh: 善湘季子汝楳，丞相史彌遠婿也，故奏報無不達。

translations.literal: Shanxiang's youngest son Rumai was the son-in-law of Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan, so memorial reports all reached their destination.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxiang's youngest son Rumai was the son-in-law of Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan, so memorial reports always reached the court.

sentences.zh: 以平閩寇功，轉江淮安撫製置使。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing bandits in Min he was transferred to Pacification and Military Commissioner of Jiang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in suppressing bandits in Min he was transferred to Pacification and Military Commissioner of Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 五年，復泰州淮安州、鹽城淮陰縣四城，及策應京湖功，進端明殿學士，與執政恩例，仍任，升留守，加食邑。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for recovering the four cities of Taizhou, Huai'an Prefecture, Yancheng, and Huaiyin County and for supporting operations in Jing-Hu, he was promoted to Academician of the Duanming Hall with the same honors as chief ministers, retained in office, elevated to Garrison Commissioner, and granted an increased fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, for recovering the four cities of Taizhou, Huai'an Prefecture, Yancheng, and Huaiyin County and for supporting operations in Jing-Hu, he was promoted to Academician of the Duanming Hall with honors equal to chief ministers, retained in office, elevated to Garrison Commissioner, and granted an increased fief.

sentences.zh: 以受金樞密副使納合買住降，復盱眙軍、泗壽二州功，進資政殿學士，加食邑，遣使賜手詔、金器等物。

translations.literal: For accepting the surrender of the Jin Deputy Director of the Privy Council Nahe Maiju and recovering Xuyi Army and the two prefectures of Si and Shou, he was promoted to Academician of the Zizheng Hall, granted an increased fief, and sent envoys bearing an imperial handwritten edict, gold vessels, and other gifts.
translations.idiomatic: For accepting the surrender of the Jin Deputy Director of the Privy Council Nahe Maiju and recovering Xuyi Army and the two prefectures of Si and Shou, he was promoted to Academician of the Zizheng Hall, granted an increased fief, and sent envoys bearing an imperial handwritten edict, gold vessels, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 九疏丐歸，皆不許。

translations.literal: He submitted nine memorials begging to retire, but none was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted nine memorials begging to retire, but none was granted.

sentences.zh: 請愈力，進大學士、提舉洞霄宮，封天水郡公，加食邑。

translations.literal: As his requests grew more forceful, he was promoted to Grand Academician and Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace, enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery, and granted an increased fief.
translations.idiomatic: As his requests grew more insistent, he was promoted to Grand Academician and Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace, enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery, and granted an increased fief.

sentences.zh: 監察御史劾奏善湘，御筆以善湘有討逆復城之功，寢其奏。

translations.literal: A Supervising Censor impeached Shanxiang. The emperor's own brush noted that Shanxiang had merit in suppressing rebellion and recovering cities, and the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: A Supervising Censor impeached Shanxiang. The emperor's own brush noted that Shanxiang had merit in suppressing rebellion and recovering cities, and the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年，授四川宣撫使兼知成都府，未拜，改沿海製置使兼知慶元府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaxi he was appointed Military Commissioner of Sichuan and concurrently prefect of Chengdu, but before assuming office was transferred to Coastal Military Commissioner and concurrently prefect of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiaxi reign (1238) he was appointed Military Commissioner of Sichuan and concurrently prefect of Chengdu, but before assuming office was transferred to Coastal Military Commissioner and concurrently prefect of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 即丐祠，改知紹興府兼浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: He immediately begged for a sinecure and was transferred to govern Shaoxing Prefecture and serve as Pacification Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately requested a sinecure and was transferred to govern Shaoxing Prefecture and serve as Pacification Commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 三年，兩請休致，四乞歸田，復提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the third year he twice requested retirement and four times begged to return to his fields. He was again made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he twice requested retirement and four times begged to return to his fields. He was again made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，帝手詔求所解《春秋》，進觀文殿學士，守本官致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou the emperor's handwritten edict sought his commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was promoted to Academician of the Guanwen Hall, retired while retaining his rank, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Chunyou reign (1242) the emperor's handwritten edict sought his commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was promoted to Academician of the Guanwen Hall, retired while retaining his rank, and died.

sentences.zh: 遺表聞，帝震悼輟視朝，贈少師，賻贈加等。

translations.literal: When his death memorial was reported, the emperor was shaken with grief and suspended court audiences. He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Preceptor, and funeral gifts were increased by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: When his death memorial was reported, the emperor was shaken with grief and suspended court audiences. He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Preceptor, and funeral gifts were increased by one grade.

sentences.zh: 所著有《周易約說》八卷，《周易或問》四卷，《周易續問》八卷，《周易指要》四卷，《學易補過》六卷，《洪範統論》一卷，《中庸約說》一卷，《大學解》十卷，《論語大意》十卷，《孟子解》十四卷，《老子解》十卷，《春秋三傳通議》三十卷，詩詞雜著三十五卷。

translations.literal: His written works include Brief Explanations of the Zhou Changes in eight juan, Questions on the Zhou Changes in four juan, Further Questions on the Zhou Changes in eight juan, Essentials of the Zhou Changes in four juan, Correcting Errors in the Study of the Changes in six juan, Comprehensive Discussion of the Great Plan in one juan, Brief Explanations of the Doctrine of the Mean in one juan, Explication of the Great Learning in ten juan, Main Points of the Analects in ten juan, Explication of Mencius in fourteen juan, Explication of Laozi in ten juan, Comprehensive Discussion of the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn in thirty juan, and miscellaneous poetry and prose in thirty-five juan.
translations.idiomatic: His written works include Brief Explanations of the Zhou Changes in eight juan, Questions on the Zhou Changes in four juan, Further Questions on the Zhou Changes in eight juan, Essentials of the Zhou Changes in four juan, Correcting Errors in the Study of the Changes in six juan, Comprehensive Discussion of the Great Plan in one juan, Brief Explanations of the Doctrine of the Mean in one juan, Explication of the Great Learning in ten juan, Main Points of the Analects in ten juan, Explication of Mencius in fourteen juan, Explication of Laozi in ten juan, Comprehensive Discussion of the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn in thirty juan, and miscellaneous poetry and prose in thirty-five juan.

sentences.zh: 趙與歡，字悅道，燕懿王八世孫。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuhuan, styled Yuedao, was an eighth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuhuan, courtesy name Yuedao, was an eighth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Yan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年進士，調會稽尉，改建寧司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Jiading, was assigned as sheriff of Kuaiji, and transferred to Revenue Assistant of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the seventh year of the Jiading reign (1214), was assigned as sheriff of Kuaiji, and transferred to Revenue Assistant of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 中明法科，攝浦城縣。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingfa examination and acted as magistrate of Pucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingfa examination and acted as magistrate of Pucheng County.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，作《善慶五規》示子孫。

translations.literal: Completing mourning for his father, he composed the Five Rules of Good Celebration to show his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his father, he composed the Five Rules of Good Celebration for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 免喪，授大理評事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 轉對，言天變、民情、國威三事，又言：“死囚以取會駁勘，動涉歲時，類瘐死，而幹證者多斃逆旅，宜精擇憲臣，悉使詳覆，果可疑則親往鞫正，必情法輕重可閔，始許審奏。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he spoke of three matters: celestial anomalies, the people's condition, and national prestige. He also said: 'Condemned prisoners, awaiting joint review and re-examination, often spend years and mostly die of illness in custody, while witnesses often die at roadside inns. Judicial officials should be carefully selected and all cases thoroughly reviewed. If truly doubtful, the official should personally go to investigate and correct the case. Only when the gravity of facts and law permits mercy should submission for review be allowed.'
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating audience he spoke of three matters: celestial anomalies, the people's condition, and national prestige. He also said, "Condemned prisoners awaiting joint review often spend years in custody and mostly die of illness, while witnesses often die at roadside inns. Judicial officials should be carefully selected and all cases thoroughly reviewed. If a case is truly doubtful, the official should personally investigate it. Only when the facts and law permit mercy should submission for review be allowed."

sentences.zh: 遷籍田令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Fields.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Fields.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜宗正寺簿，曆軍器監、司農寺丞，遷宗正丞兼權都官郎官，改倉部，權度支，以直寶章閣知安吉州。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, served successively as Superintendent of the Armory and Assistant Director of Agriculture in the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent acting appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to the Grain Bureau, given acting appointment in the Budget Bureau, and made Direct Attendant of the Baozhang Pavilion and prefect of Anji.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, served as Superintendent of the Armory and Assistant Director of Agriculture in the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent acting appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to the Grain Bureau, given acting appointment in the Budget Bureau, and made Direct Attendant of the Baozhang Pavilion and prefect of Anji.

sentences.zh: 郡計仰榷醋，禁綱峻密，與歡首捐以予民。

translations.literal: The prefecture's revenue depended on the vinegar monopoly, whose regulations were strict and dense. Yuhuan was the first to remit it and give it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's revenue depended on the vinegar monopoly, whose regulations were strict and burdensome. Yuhuan was the first to remit it and give the benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 設銅鉦縣門，欲訴者擊之，冤無不直。

translations.literal: He set up a bronze gong at the county gate; those wishing to plead their case would strike it, and no injustice went uncorrected.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a bronze gong at the county gate; anyone wishing to plead a case could strike it, and no injustice went uncorrected.

sentences.zh: 有富民訴幼子，察之非其本心，姑逮其子付獄，徐廉之，乃二兄強其父析業。

translations.literal: A wealthy man sued his youngest son. Yuhuan perceived this was not from his true heart. He temporarily detained the son and placed him in prison, then gradually investigated and found that the two elder brothers had forced their father to divide the estate.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man sued his youngest son. Yuhuan saw that this was not the father's true wish. He temporarily detained the son, then gradually investigated and found that the two elder brothers had forced their father to divide the estate.

sentences.zh: 與歡曉以法，開以天理，皆忻然感悟。

translations.literal: Yuhuan enlightened them with law and opened them with heavenly principle. All gladly came to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhuan explained the law to them and appealed to natural justice. All came to understanding with glad hearts.

sentences.zh: 又嫠媼僅一子，亦以不孝告，留之郡聽，日給饌，俾親饋，晨昏以禮，未周月，母子如初。
